text: Welcome to our workshop. Today we are walking through the tools we used to plan our first launch. We'll cover the production calendar, the packaging samples, and the steps we took to get ready for our first customer orders.

Here is the mistake that cost us a week. We booked the photographer before we approved the packaging, so a single label change invalidated half the shot list. Next time, start with the packaging approval and make every downstream booking depend on that milestone.

We keep our planning notes in one folder. We share each new version at the weekly check-in and archive the old versions together. The folder is also where we log decisions about photos and print materials.

Try this before renting more storage. Put the items you reach for every day in one tray, then move the rest out of arm's reach. The reason this works is that your next action gets easier. Start with one shelf and measure how often you need to reach past something.

The biggest lesson from our launch was simple. A deadline means little until someone owns it. Every Monday, write down the task, the person, and what must happen first. If you cannot name all three, make that uncertainty visible before you schedule work around it.
